title: 2019 AMC 12A Problem 7
statement: Melanie computes the mean \(\mu,\) the median \(M,\) and the modes of the \(365\) values that are the dates in the months of \(2019.\) Thus her data consist of \(12\) \(1\)s, \(12\) \(2\)s, \(\ldots,\) \(12\) \(28\)s, \(11\) \(29\)s, \(11\) \(30\)s, and \(7\) \(31\)s. Let \(d\) be the median of the modes. Which of the following statements is true?

solutions.text:
The values \(1\) through \(28\) each appear \(12\) times and are the modes, so \(d = \dfrac{14 + 15}{2} = 14.5.\)

The \(183\)rd of the \(365\) ordered values is the median. Values \(1\) through \(15\) fill the first \(180\) positions, so position \(183\) is \(16;\) thus \(M = 16.\)

The total of all values is \(12(1 + \cdots + 28)\) \(+ 11(29 + 30)\) \(+ 7 \cdot 31 = 5738,\) so \(\mu = \dfrac{5738}{365} \approx 15.7.\)

Therefore \(d \lt \mu \lt M.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The modes are \(1\) through \(28,\) each appearing \(12\) times, so \(d\) is their median
The median \(M\) is the \(183\)rd value; compute \(\mu\) directly from the totals
